questions.questionText: Six friends B, D, A, F, C, E are sitting in a straight row facing North. D is to the immediate right of B. A is sitting third to the left of E. F is between A and C. B is at the extreme left end. Who is sitting at the extreme right end?
questions.hint: When facing North, your left is the line's left and your right is the line's right.
questions.explanation: From the clues, B is at the extreme left end. The linear order from left to right is: B - D - A - F - C - E. Therefore, E sits at the extreme right end.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Fix the definite positions (e.g. extreme ends).
Step 2: Place immediate neighbors and relative offsets.
Step 3: Verify all conditions against the deduced order: B - D - A - F - C - E.
questions.memoryTip: Facing North: Left = West, Right = East. Leftmost end is position 1.

questions.hint: Caution: When persons face South, their left is our right, and their right is our left.
questions.explanation: When facing South, direction orientation inverts. The order from right to left is F -> A -> E -> C -> D -> B. The person at the extreme left end is B.
solutionSteps: Step 1: Note the orientation: facing South inverts left/right perspective.
Step 2: Trace from their rightmost position (F) towards their left.
Step 3: The extreme left end is occupied by B.
questions.memoryTip: Facing South Rule: "Left" moves rightwards on your notebook; "Right" moves leftwards.
